name: KX2
subtitle: Field reference
kicker: Independent reference. Not an Elecraft publication and not affiliated with Elecraft.
verified: Compiled from the Elecraft KX2 Owner's Manual rev B2 and the Elecraft product page, September 2026. Not checked against a radio.
specs: USB, LSB, CW and data, with PSK31, PSK63 and RTTY built in
10 W on 80 through 17 m, 8 W on 12 and 10 m, per the product page
9 to 15 V at the DC jack. Full SSB output wants 12 V or better
About 150 mA with the backlight and preamp off
About 13 oz bare, without battery or options
ACC jack, 3.5 mm, serial through a KXUSB or KXSER cable
keys: RATE + A/B
Held together about two seconds, this is the power switch. There is no separate one.
RATE / FREQ
Tap steps the tuning rate. Hold for direct frequency entry.
MODE / RCL
Tap changes mode. Hold enters memory recall, longer starts a scan.
BAND / STORE
Tap changes band. Hold stores a memory.
A/B / A>B
Tap swaps the VFOs. Hold copies A into B.
RIT / SPLIT
Tap toggles receive incremental tuning. Hold toggles split.
DISP / MENU
Tap cycles the alternate displays. Hold opens the menu.
XMIT / TUNE
Tap keys the transmitter. Hold sends a carrier for tuning.
ATU / PFn
Tap runs or selects the tuner. Hold reaches the programmable function.
PRE / NR
Tap toggles the preamp. Hold turns on noise reduction.
FIL / APF
Tap enters filter adjust. Hold gives the audio peaking filter on CW, or auto notch on SSB and AM.
DATA / TEXT
Tap selects data mode and sub-mode. Hold opens the decode display.
MSG / REC
Tap plays a stored message. Hold records one.
AF / MON
Receive audio level. The alternate function is monitor level.
KYR / MIC
Keyer speed on CW, mic gain on voice. Hold it to reach the power setting.
quick: Turns AGC off so RF gain can be set by hand. The icon changes to AGC minus.
Slow or fast. Fast is the default on CW, slow elsewhere.
Manual receiver gain, for use with AGC off.
Set so VOX triggers on normal speech, not on the dog.
filters: Tap FIL to enter filter adjust. AF sets width, KYR shifts the passband, tapping AF normalises to the standard setting for the mode.
Hold FIL on CW for a very narrow audio peak. Weak signal work only.
Hold FIL on SSB or AM to pull down a steady carrier.
Noise blanker, for repetitive noise: power line, appliance, ignition. Use the lowest setting that works.
Noise reduction, for hiss. It sounds hollow, and high settings eat weak signals.
tasks: Hold STORE, rotate VFO A to the channel number, hold STORE again to commit. Any other key abandons it.
Hold RCL, pick the memory with VFO A, tap any key to leave.
Put the start and end frequencies in VFO A and B, store that as a memory, recall it, then hold RCL about three seconds until SCAN appears. It stops on a modulated signal.
Hold A>B twice so B matches A, tune B to the offset, then hold SPLIT. The TX icon moves to VFO B.
Hold the KYR / MIC knob to bring up PWR, then rotate.
control: ACC, 3.5 mm stereo, on the left side
KXUSB for a computer USB port, KXSER for a real RS-232 port. A bare cable will not do.
Set with the BR command. The choices are 4800, 9600, 19200 and 38400. Write yours below.
Firmware updates and the KXPA100 amplifier.
notes: Thirteen ounces is the whole argument for this radio. If the rest of the kit is not chosen to match, the weight saving goes back into the pack somewhere else.
Receive current in the low hundreds of milliamps means a small battery lasts a long day, as long as you are not transmitting flat out for all of it.
The internal tuner is an option. Know whether yours has one before you plan an antenna that depends on it.
Elecraft's manual and product page disagree on maximum output. Set the power you actually use, measure it once, and write it below.
Log the output you used. On a radio with this range, five watts and ten watts are different activations.
